### Observed differences

- In the later window, the relative order of two groups of activities reversed. Activities A20, A21, A23 and A24 moved from around 63% of the trace length to around 40%; activities A19, A22, A25 and A26 moved from around 32–35% to around 68–69%. [POS002, POS003, POS005, POS006, POS001, POS004, POS007, POS008]
- Pairwise order relations confirm this: before, A27 and A31 preceded A20/A21/A23/A24 in about 98–100% of traces; after, A20/A21/A23/A24 precede A27/A31 in about 97–99% of traces. Similarly, A22/A25/A26 preceded A20/A21/A23/A24 before, and now follow them. [REL010, REL011, REL015, REL016, REL023, REL024, REL027, REL028, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL025, REL026, REL029, REL030, REL031, REL032]
- Successor routing changed around A27 and A32. In the later window, A19, A22, A25 and A26 go to A32 in about 95–98% of their outgoing transitions, where before they went to A27; A20, A21, A23 and A24 now go to A27 in about 21–28% of transitions, where before they went to A32 in about 21–26%. [DIR001, DIR004, DIR007, DIR008, DIR002, DIR003, DIR005, DIR006]
- A31's successors changed from A20/A21/A23/A24 to A19/A22/A25/A26; A42's successors changed from A19/A22/A25/A26 to A20/A21/A23/A24. [DIR009, DIR010]
- Lag distances show A32 moved from being within 1–4 steps of A20/A21/A23/A24 in most traces to being absent from those pairs (only 1–2 traces within 5 steps), and closer to A26 and A31. [LAG001, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG011]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the process was restructured so that the order of two groups of activities reversed, with A20, A21, A23 and A24 now occurring earlier and A19, A22, A25 and A26 occurring later, while routing through A27 and A32 changed accordingly. The successor changes are consistent with this reordering: A19/A22/A25/A26 now lead to A32, while A20/A21/A23/A24 now lead to A27. [POS002, POS003, POS005, POS006, POS001, POS004, POS007, POS008, REL010, REL011, REL015, REL016, REL023, REL024, REL027, REL028, DIR001, DIR004, DIR007, DIR008, DIR002, DIR003, DIR005, DIR006]

The number of qualifying evidence items (66) is far above the 0.81 expected by chance, and the pattern is consistent across positional, relational, successor and lag indicators. A competing explanation that the differences are just sampling variation in variant frequencies is unlikely given the size and consistency of the changes, though the finite samples cannot rule out some contribution from rare variants. [screening, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, LAG001, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG011]
